name: What Went Wrong?
summary: Flat cookies, cakey brownies, a sunken loaf, tough pancakes: the usual causes and what to change next time.

rows: Spread thin and flat
Butter too soft or melted; too little flour; dough put on a warm sheet; oven not fully hot.
Use softened, not warm, butter; [measure flour](guide:measuring-for-baking) carefully; chill the dough 30 minutes; cool sheets between batches.
Puffy and cakey
Too much flour (scooped cups); too much creaming or too many eggs.
Spoon and level the flour, or weigh it; cream just until light.
Dark or burnt bottoms
Dark baking sheet; rack too low; oven runs hot.
Light sheet lined with parchment, middle rack, check your oven with a thermometer ([Oven and Pans](guide:oven-and-pans)).
Dry and hard
Overbaked, or too much flour.
Take them out while the centers still look soft.
Uneven batch
Different-sized scoops; hot spots in the oven.
Use a scoop or tablespoon; turn the sheet halfway.

blocks.text: The [Chocolate Chip Cookies](recipe:chocolate-chip-cookies) tips explain chilling the dough for thicker cookies.

rows: Cakey instead of fudgy
Overbaked; too much flour; too much beating after the flour went in.
Pull them when a toothpick shows moist crumbs; fold the flour in gently.
No shiny, crackly top
Eggs and sugar not beaten enough.
Beat the eggs and sugar hard for a minute, as the [Fudgy Brownies](recipe:brownies) tip says.
Dry edges, raw middle
Glass or dark pan; the recipe's full batter in a smaller pan, so it's deeper.
Use a light metal pan, or lower the oven by 25°F (15°C) and bake longer ([pan size](guide:oven-and-pans#size)).
Crumble when cut
Cut while warm.
Cool completely in the pan first.
Sank in the middle
Underbaked; too much baking soda or powder; oven door opened too early.
Check doneness with a skewer, not the clock; measure leaveners with level spoons.
Tough, with tunnels and peaked tops
Overmixed after the flour went in.
Stir only until no dry flour shows ([muffin method](guide:mixing-methods#muffin-method)).
Gummy streak near the bottom
Underbaked, or too much wet ingredient (very big bananas).
Bake until a skewer is clean; measure mashed banana if your bananas are large.
Dark top, raw center
Oven too hot, or a dark pan.
Lay foil loosely over the top once it's brown, as in the [Banana Bread](recipe:banana-bread) tip.
Dense and heavy
Old leavener; too much flour.
[Test](guide:baking-ingredients#leaveners) your baking soda and powder; weigh the flour.

sections.heading: Pancakes

rows: Flat and dense
Old baking powder; overmixed batter; batter left standing a long time.
Test the baking powder; stir until just combined; cook within about 15 minutes.
Tough or rubbery
Overmixed.
Lumpy batter is right.
Burnt outside, raw inside
Pan too hot.
Medium heat; the first pancake is a test.
Pale and greasy
Pan not hot enough, or too much butter in the pan.
Heat the pan longer; brush on a thin layer of butter.
